summary: Sudden 5xx spike tied to HTTP/2 stream window exhaustion and runtime kernel-fallback restarts
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-09 23:12 UTC and 2026-03-10 00:05 UTC ScribeFlow observed an abrupt increase in 502/503 responses for streaming sessions. Impact: customer streaming sessions terminated mid-response and some long polls returned 5xx; total token throughput for tenant dropped ~60% during the window. Scope: affected a single dedicated tenant (ScribeFlow) in us-west-2 running mostly streaming chat workloads against redwood-small-v1. Initial hypothesis: apigw connection limits or backend overload. See investigation notes below for the chain-of-failure and mitigation applied.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a multiplexed HTTP/2 client to open ~30 concurrent server-push style streaming sessions to the tenant endpoint
2) Send sustained traffic with ~80% of requests using long-lived streaming (keepalive interval > 60s)
3) Observe that after ~2 minutes the apigw reports increased stream resets (RST_STREAM) and client sees 502/503
4) On backend runtimes monitor for kernel fallback logs and watchdog restarts
logs: apigw-2026-03-09T23:14:12Z ERROR http2: RST_STREAM code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM tenant_id=scribeflow stream_id=17
runtime-2026-03-09T23:14:16Z WARN kernel-fallback: quant-kernel-probe failed => falling back to scalar kernel; latency spike observed: 1.2s
runtime-2026-03-09T23:15:02Z ERROR watchdog: no-progress timeout; sending SIGABRT to worker pid=4128
investigation_notes: 23:20 UTC - Support (Priya) triaged and confirmed 5xx increase on customer's tenant via tenant-level metrics and request traces.
23:25 UTC - SRE (Ben) pulled apigw logs: pattern of RST_STREAM and connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE drops coincident with tenant burst of multiplexed streams.

23:30 UTC - Runtime team observed repeated kernel-probe failures when a memory/CPU scheduling jitter occurred; runtime switched execution path to slower scalar kernels which increased latency and triggered watchdog no-progress timers.
23:35 UTC - Feedback loop: increased latency led apigw backpressure and stream window stalls; stalled streams accumulated, causing connection reset amplification and client-visible 502/503.

Root cause (combined): a) tenant's high-multiplexing streaming pattern exhausted HTTP/2 stream/window resources at apigw and b) a recent runtime kernel probing change (PR 12634) caused intermittent fallback to slower kernels under brief memory pressure which amplified tail latency and then triggered watchdog restarts.
Evidence: correlated timestamps between apigw RST_STREAMs, runtime kernel-fallback logs, and watchdog restarts; CPU and heap traces from the affected runtimes captured rapid kernel-probe activity.
Reproducibility: reliably repro'd in staging when simulating multiplexed long-lived streams and toggling kernel-probe experimental flag.
comments: 2026-03-10T00:01Z Priya Desai: Customer reports clients see truncated streaming responses and automatic reconnects. Asked them to reduce concurrent streams as workaround.
2026-03-10T00:12Z Ben Morales (SRE): Found apigw logs showing excessive RST_STREAM for tenant; runtime logs show repeated 'kernel-fallback' messages timed with RSTs.
2026-03-10T01:00Z Runtime Eng (Hannah Li): We rolled back PR 12634 to canary and observed immediate reduction in kernel-fallback events on canary hosts.
2026-03-10T01:45Z Ben Morales: Applied apigw tuning to lower per-connection concurrency and increased WINDOW_UPDATE thresholds for tenant's route as temporary mitigation.
2026-03-10T02:10Z Priya Desai: Customer confirmed streaming error rate dropped to baseline after mitigations; continuing to monitor for 24h.
2026-03-11T09:30Z Ben Morales: Postmortem draft created and follow-ups assigned; marking ticket resolved after 24h healthy observation window.
resolution: Immediate fix: rolled back experimental kernel-probing change (PR 12634) from dedicated runtime pool and applied apigw tuning (reduced max concurrent streams for tenant route, raised connection window thresholds). Workaround given to customer: reduce concurrent multiplexed streams to <=8 and enable shorter keepalive intervals. Long-term actions: add guard to disable kernel-probing under memory jitter, harden runtime watchdog thresholds to avoid cascade restarts, add apigw per-tenant streaming quotas and a playbook for HTTP/2 window stalls. Follow-up tasks created in INT-4021 and a runtime PR to add probesafe mode.
follow_up_actions: Create a dedicated runbook for HTTP/2 stream window exhaustion (owner: SRE)
Add automated test in CI that simulates multiplexed streaming to detect window-starvation regressions (owner: runtime team)
Implement 'probesafe' flag to avoid kernel-probing under low-memory jitter and add telemetry (owner: runtime)
Convene postmortem w/ customer + eng to review changes and SLA impact (owner: Support)
Schedule apigw capacity audit for tenant routing rules (owner: infra)
